title: Accepting a bike shop job
passage: Subject: Offer of employment: Customer Service Associate
Dear Ms. Okafor,

Thank you for interviewing with us last Thursday. It was a pleasure to meet you, and everyone at Harbourline Cycle Works was impressed by your enthusiasm and by your experience helping customers in your previous retail position.

I am delighted to offer you the part-time position of Customer Service Associate at our Halifax shop. The job starts on Monday, March 3, and involves 24 hours of work per week, usually from Thursday to Saturday. The hourly wage is $18.50. After a three-month probation period, you will be eligible for a staff discount of 25 percent on bicycles and accessories.

During your first week, you will complete paid training with our assistant manager, Dev Malhotra. He will show you how to use our point-of-sale system, how to book repair appointments and how to handle returns. Please plan to arrive at 8:45 a.m. on your first day so that we can finish your paperwork before the shop opens at 9:30.

To accept this offer, please sign the attached letter and return it to me by Friday, February 21. If your availability changes before your start date, let me know as soon as possible, because we would need to adjust the weekly schedule. Please also bring two pieces of identification, one with your photo, and your banking details for direct deposit.
A small note about getting to work: we do not have staff parking behind the shop, but bus route 14 stops right at the corner of Quinpool Road and Preston Street.
We look forward to welcoming you to the team. Please call me at 902-555-0147 if you have any questions about the schedule or benefits.
Sincerely,
Priya Raman
Store Manager, Harbourline Cycle Works

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Priya’s email?
o: To offer Ms. Okafor a job and explain the details
To invite Ms. Okafor to a second interview
To announce a sale at the bike shop
To ask Ms. Okafor for references
questions.e: The email begins “I am delighted to offer you the part-time position” and then gives the start date, hours, wage and next steps.

questions.q: When will Ms. Okafor become eligible for the staff discount?
o: On her first day of work
After her first week of training
After she signs the attached letter
questions.e: The email says the discount applies “after a three-month probation period.”

questions.q: What must Ms. Okafor do by February 21?
o: Bring two pieces of identification to the shop
Sign the attached letter and return it
questions.e: Priya asks her to “sign the attached letter and return it to me by Friday, February 21.” The identification is requested later, with no stated deadline.

questions.q: In the second paragraph, the phrase “eligible for” is closest in meaning to:
questions.e: Being “eligible for a staff discount” means she will be allowed or qualified to receive it.

questions.q: Why does Priya mention bus route 14?
o: Because the shop runs a free shuttle
Because staff cannot park behind the shop
Because the shop is far from downtown
Because Ms. Okafor asked about transit
questions.e: She says there is no staff parking and then points out the bus stop at the corner, implying public transit is the practical way to get there.

questions.q: Which word best describes the tone of the email?
questions.e: The email is polite and organized (“delighted,” “welcoming you to the team”) while staying businesslike.

title: Cedar Street block party
passage: Subject: You’re invited: Cedar Street block party on September 14!
Hi neighbours,

I hope you’re enjoying the last of the summer weather. A few of us have been talking about how little we see of each other, so we’ve decided to do something about it: the first-ever Cedar Street block party is happening on Saturday, September 14, from 2:00 to 7:00 p.m.

The city has approved our permit, which means Cedar Street will be closed to traffic between 4th and 6th Avenue for the afternoon. To keep everyone safe, please move your vehicles off the street before 10:00 a.m. that morning. Cars left on the street after that time may be towed, and none of us wants to start a party with a tow truck.

The Hendersons have kindly offered to lend us their big barbecue and will be grilling burgers and veggie patties. Everything else will be a potluck, so please bring a dish to share. Let me know what you plan to make when you reply, so that we don’t end up with eight potato salads. One request: please keep the dishes nut-free, since one of our young neighbours has a serious allergy.

There will be face painting at 3:00 for the kids and relay races at 4:00 for anyone who’s feeling competitive, including the grown-ups. Bring your own chairs, and a sweater in case the evening gets cool. If it rains, we’ll move everything to the gym at Fernhill Elementary School, which the principal has generously allowed us to use.
I’m also looking for a few volunteers: three people to help set up tables at 12:30, and three to help with cleanup after 7:00. If you can help, just mention it in your reply.
Please RSVP by Saturday, September 7, by replying to this email with your name, the number of people coming and the dish you’ll bring. I can’t wait to finally meet everyone properly!
Cheers,
Marisol Vega
42 Cedar Street

questions.q: Why is Marisol writing to her neighbours?
o: To complain about traffic on Cedar Street
To announce that a new permit is required
To ask for donations for a school
To invite them to a block party and ask for some help
questions.e: She invites everyone to the party and also asks for dishes, volunteers and RSVPs.

questions.q: What should residents do with their vehicles?
o: Park them in the school gym
Leave them in place until 2:00 p.m.
Move them off the street before 10:00 a.m.
Give the keys to the Hendersons
questions.e: The email asks for vehicles to be moved “before 10:00 a.m.” and warns that cars left later may be towed.

questions.q: Where will the party be held if the weather is bad?
questions.e: The email says “If it rains, we’ll move everything to the gym at Fernhill Elementary School.”

questions.q: In the third paragraph, what does “potluck” mean?
o: A meal where guests bring food to share
A meal prepared by one family
questions.e: Marisol explains that everything except the grilled food is a potluck, so “bring a dish to share.”

questions.q: Why does Marisol ask people to tell her what dish they will bring?
o: To avoid having too many of the same dish
To decide who will do the cooking
To check for nuts in every recipe
To count how many chairs are needed
questions.e: Her joke about “eight potato salads” shows she wants variety. The nut-free request is a separate point.

questions.q: Which best describes the tone of the email?
questions.e: She uses a chatty, friendly style (“Hi neighbours,” “Cheers,” jokes about a tow truck).

title: A delayed dining set
passage: Subject: Order #MH-48213: damaged and incomplete delivery
To the Customer Care Team,

I am writing about a dining set I ordered from Maplewood Home Furnishings on September 19. At checkout I was told that the table and six chairs would arrive by October 10. They actually arrived on October 24, and only after four phone calls from me, none of which produced a clear explanation for the delay.

The condition of the delivery was, unfortunately, a further disappointment. The oak tabletop has a long scratch across the centre, and only four of the six chairs were in the boxes. The delivery crew spent perhaps fifteen minutes in my home, and when I pointed out the damage, they suggested I contact the store. I have photographs of the scratch and of the packing slip, which lists six chairs, and I can send these on request.

When I called again on October 25, a representative named Karen offered to refund the $79 delivery fee. While I appreciate the gesture, it addresses only the lateness. It does nothing about a damaged table or the two chairs I paid for and still do not have. I should add that Karen was courteous throughout; my concern is with the process, not with her.

I have been a customer for some time. My sofa, bought two years ago, has given me no trouble, which is exactly why this experience has been so surprising. I had expected a company I trusted to handle a problem like this without my having to chase it.

I would therefore like the company to do the following: replace the damaged tabletop, deliver the two missing chairs at no charge, and apply a reasonable discount to reflect the three-week delay and the inconvenience. I would be grateful for a written reply within seven business days.

If we cannot reach a satisfactory arrangement by then, I will be prepared to escalate the matter, first by disputing the charge with my credit card company and then by contacting the provincial consumer protection office. I would very much prefer not to take that step.
Yours sincerely,
Daniel Whitfield

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Daniel’s email?
o: To praise a customer service employee
To ask when his sofa will arrive
To request a fair solution to a faulty delivery
questions.e: He describes the late, damaged and incomplete delivery, then lists the remedies he wants.

questions.q: Which problems did Daniel find when the set arrived?
o: A broken chair and a missing table leg
A late crew and a wrong colour
A scratched tabletop and two missing chairs
A missing packing slip and a torn box
questions.e: He reports a scratch on the oak tabletop and only four of six chairs. The packing slip was present because he has a photograph of it.

questions.q: Why does Daniel say the $79 refund is not enough?
o: It is smaller than the price of a chair
It does not address the damage or the missing chairs
It was offered by a rude employee
It arrived after the seven-day deadline
questions.e: He says the refund “addresses only the lateness” and does nothing about the table or the chairs. He also states Karen was courteous.

questions.q: In the final paragraph, “escalate the matter” most nearly means:
o: take the problem to higher authorities
questions.e: He then lists the credit card dispute and consumer protection office, which are steps up in seriousness.

questions.q: Why does Daniel mention his sofa?
o: To show he is a loyal customer who expected better
To ask for a refund on the sofa
To prove the company makes weak furniture
To suggest that Karen was unprofessional
questions.e: He says the sofa gave no trouble, which is “exactly why” this experience surprised him, so he is presenting himself as a trusting customer.

questions.q: Which best describes the tone of the email?
questions.e: He sets clear demands and a deadline but acknowledges Karen’s courtesy and says he prefers not to escalate.

title: Notice of building maintenance
passage: Subject: Important notice: Water shut-off and parking changes at Birchwood Court
Dear residents,

We are writing to let you know about three pieces of maintenance work that will affect the building in November. We regret any inconvenience and have tried to keep the disruption as short as possible.

First, the municipal water department will be replacing a main valve on Birchwood Avenue. As a result, water to the entire building will be shut off on Tuesday, November 12, from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Because the crew has been scheduled by the city rather than by us, we are unable to change the date. We suggest filling a few containers beforehand for drinking and flushing. Residents who need to shower that morning may use the Eastgate Fitness Centre, two blocks away, free of charge by showing a Birchwood Court key fob at the front desk.

Second, following the valve work, a plumber will inspect the pipes in suites 301 to 312 on Wednesday, November 13, between 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. This notice constitutes the written notice of entry required by provincial tenancy rules. If you will not be home, a staff member will let the plumber in with a master key unless you tell the office otherwise by Friday, November 8. Please put away anything fragile or valuable near the sinks and bathtubs.

Finally, Lot B at the rear of the building will be repaved from Monday, November 18, to Wednesday, November 20. All vehicles must be removed by 7:00 a.m. on November 18. The city has agreed to waive its overnight parking restrictions on Cartier Street for those three nights, so residents may park there without a permit. Vehicles left in Lot B during the work will be towed at the owner’s expense.
We appreciate your patience and cooperation. Questions can be directed to the building office, which is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or to office@birchwoodcourt.example.
Sincerely,
Ruth Abelard
Property Manager, Birchwood Court

questions.q: What is the main purpose of this notice?
o: To ask residents to vote on repairs
To inform tenants about upcoming work and what they must do
To introduce a new property manager
questions.e: The notice describes a water shut-off, a pipe inspection and a repaving project, each with instructions.

questions.q: Why can’t the water shut-off be moved to another date?
o: The plumber is away on holiday
The city’s crew has been scheduled by the municipality
Lot B must be repaved first
questions.e: The notice says the crew was “scheduled by the city rather than by us,” so management cannot change the date.

questions.q: What will happen if the resident of suite 305 is out on November 13 and has not contacted the office?
o: The plumber will return on November 14
A staff member will let the plumber in
questions.e: A staff member will admit the plumber with a master key unless the tenant says otherwise by November 8.

questions.q: In the fourth paragraph, “waive” is closest in meaning to:
questions.e: If the city waives its parking restrictions, it is not applying them temporarily, which lets residents park without a permit.

questions.q: Why does the notice mention Eastgate Fitness Centre?
o: To suggest a new place to park
To announce a gym opening at Birchwood Court
To give directions to the city office
To offer a free place for residents to shower
questions.e: Residents who need to shower while the water is off may use the centre free of charge with their key fob.

questions.q: Which best describes the tone of the notice?
questions.e: The language is official (“constitutes the written notice”) but includes apologies, practical help and thanks.

title: Reply about a laptop warranty claim
passage: Subject: Re: Warranty claim for Brightwave Slate 14, serial BW-77120
Dear Mr. Chen,

Thank you for your message of November 2, and for sending the laptop to our service centre in Mississauga. I am sorry for the frustration you have experienced, and I would like to explain the results of our assessment as clearly as I can.

Our technicians found two separate issues. The first is the battery, which no longer holds a proper charge. This is a manufacturing fault, and it is fully covered by your two-year limited warranty. We will replace it at no cost to you and have attached a prepaid shipping label for the return.

The second issue is the cracked screen. The pattern of the damage, including the pressure marks around the lower-left corner, indicates that the laptop was struck or squeezed rather than that the panel was defective. Our warranty excludes accidental damage, and I am therefore unable to approve this part of your claim. I know this is not the answer you were hoping for, and I do not take that lightly.

As a courtesy, and in recognition of the fact that your laptop is only fourteen months old, we are prepared to make a one-time exception. We can replace the screen for $149, which is less than half our usual repair rate of $310. Alternatively, you may take a 15 percent coupon toward the purchase of any new Brightwave laptop. The coupon, like the reduced repair price, is valid until December 15.

If you would like the screen repaired, you need only reply to this email, and we will carry out both repairs together to save you time. If you prefer the coupon, we will return the laptop to you with the new battery installed and send the coupon code separately.
Please contact me directly with any questions.
Kind regards,
Julia Navarro
Customer Support Specialist, Brightwave Electronics

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Julia’s email?
o: To ask Mr. Chen to buy extended coverage
To announce a recall of the Slate 14
To explain the warranty decision and offer options
To apologize for losing his laptop
questions.e: She reports the findings, says which fault is covered, and then presents a reduced-price repair or a coupon.

questions.q: Which problem is covered by the warranty?
questions.e: The battery is “a manufacturing fault” covered by the warranty, while the screen damage is excluded.

questions.q: Why was the screen claim not approved?
o: The damage appears to be accidental, which the warranty excludes
The warranty expired fourteen months ago
The screen was never sent to the service centre
The technicians could not find any damage
questions.e: Pressure marks suggest the laptop was struck or squeezed, and the warranty “excludes accidental damage.” The laptop is within the two-year warranty period.

questions.q: In the fourth paragraph, “as a courtesy” suggests that the offer is:
o: a legal duty of the company
a favour the company is not required to give
questions.e: A courtesy is something done out of politeness or goodwill, not because it is obligatory; the company has just said the screen is excluded from warranty.

questions.q: What does the expression “one-time exception” most likely imply?
o: The laptop will be replaced for free
The offer applies to all customers
The coupon can be used repeatedly
The offer should not be expected again in future claims
questions.e: “One-time” signals that this is a special arrangement, not a new policy, so a similar request later may be refused.

questions.q: Which best describes Julia’s tone?
questions.e: She expresses regret and offers alternatives, yet maintains her decision on the screen.
